title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Sophie Martinez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the core company-handbook topics new and existing employees refer to most often: how we work at Redwood, our roles and career ladder philosophy, benefits & perks, a hiring & onboarding overview, and the most-used internal tools and first-day checklist. It is intended to be a stable, broadly consumable reference maintained by People Ops (owner: people-ops).

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Short intro: Redwood is an engineering-first company that values ownership, reliability, collaboration, and measurable impact. We are distributed across North America, Europe, and APAC; most teams follow a hybrid/remote-first approach unless otherwise specified.

Core principles:
- Customer-first engineering: prioritize production-readiness, cost-consciousness, and reliability in every design.
- Ship small, iterate fast: small, observable rollouts with clear rollback/fallback plans.
- Psychological safety and blameless postmortems: focus on learning, not blame.
- Inclusive communication: async-first; use Confluence & Slack for cross-timezone collaboration.

Working norms and practical expectations:
- Core hours: teams establish local overlap windows; a typical expectation is 10:00-15:00 local team time for synchronous collaboration.
- Meeting hygiene: add an agenda, desired outcome, and pre-read for any meeting >15 minutes.
- On-call: many infra and platform engineers participate in a shared on-call roster; see the oncall-and-incident-response runbooks for SLOs and rotation details.

2) Roles & career ladders

Overview: Redwood uses a competency-based leveling framework for individual contributors (ICs) and managers. The goal is clarity of growth, predictable expectations, and fair compensation.

Common career tracks:
- Individual Contributor (IC) track: IC1 / IC2 / IC3 / Senior / Staff / Principal
- Engineering Manager (EM) track: EM1 / EM2 / Senior Manager / Director
- Product & Design: PM1–PM4, Designer I–III, Lead Designer
- Cross-functional: Solutions/Customer Success, Sales, Security, People Ops with parallel leveling scales.

Promotion & leveling guidelines (summary):
- Promotions are based on demonstrated impact, scope increase, technical or cross-functional leadership, and consistent competency against the rubric.
- Cadence: managers discuss promotions in biannual calibration cycles (typically May and November) and ad-hoc promotions are permitted with cross-functional sign-off.
- Evidence: promotion packets should include 3-6 concrete examples mapped to the rubric, peer feedback, and counterfactuals (what would need to change to deny promotion).

Example expectations by level (high level):
| Level | Focus | Typical scope | Impact measures |
|-------|-------|--------------|----------------|
| IC2 | Strong execution | Feature-area ownership; mentor juniors | Delivery quality, shipping predictably |
| Senior | Technical leadership | Multi-team projects, design ownership | Initiative impact, mentorship, and design quality |
| Staff | Strategic influence | Cross-product initiatives | Systemic improvements, hiring and roadmap influence |

Compensation & performance reviews:
- Annual compensation review in Q1 aligned with performance cycle. Promotional salary adjustments outside cycle are possible and typically effective within 30 days of approval.
- Performance review cadence: annual review + mid-year calibration for managers.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Health & wellbeing:
- Medical, dental, and vision plans (company covers majority of premium for employees; details in Benefits portal).
- Mental health support: EAP and 8 therapy sessions covered per year.
- Wellness stipend: $200 / quarter for equipment, classes, or subscriptions.

Paid time off & parental leave:
- Vacation: flexible policy with recommended minimum of 15 days per year; managers work with ICs to ensure coverage.
- Public holidays: regional holiday calendar maintained in Confluence.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver paid leave; 8 weeks secondary caregiver paid leave.
- Care & bereavement: compassionate leave policies detailed in Benefits portal.

Financial & equity:
- 401(k) / pension: company match up to plan limit (see Benefits portal for details).
- Equity: RSU/equity grants per role and level; refresh grants at manager discretion during performance cycles.

Learning & career support:
- Learning stipend: $1,500 per year for courses, conferences, and books.
- Mentorship program and career coaching offered through People Ops.

Workspace & equipment:
- Home office stipend: $1,000 one-time new-hire stipend; ergonomic equipment reimbursement thereafter.
- Global co-working allowance for teams that request in-region workspaces.

Other perks:
- Commuter benefits in supported regions, discounted partner services, regular All-Hands, and team social budgets.

How to access benefits:
- Link: Confluence > company-handbook > Benefits (also available in the HR Benefits portal). For policy exceptions, contact benefits@redwood.com.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring principles:
- Hire for high bar and cultural add. We aim for diverse, technical hires who prioritize customer impact.
- Interview loops are competency-based, evidence-focused, and consistent across candidates.

Standard interview loop (engineering):
1. Recruiter screen (30-45 min): role fit, compensation band, logistics.
2. Technical screen (45-60 min): coding or system design (role-dependent).
3. Onsite / virtual loop (3-5 interviews): mix of coding, systems design, and cross-functional interviews.
4. Hiring committee review: packet with rubric scores and hiring manager recommendation.
5. Offer and reference checks.

Interview rubric highlights:
- Evaluated dimensions: problem solving, technical depth, product sense, communication, and team fit.
- Use the standardized rubric template (Confluence: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/interview-rubric) for scoring.

Offer & onboarding process (first 30 days):
- Offer approval: hiring manager collects compensation, equity, and sign-off from Finance and People Ops.
- Background check: initiated after offer acceptance per regional compliance.
- First-day setup: hardware order placed by People Ops; accounts provisioned (Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub).

First-day / first-week checklist (numbered):
1. Complete HR intake and benefits enrollment.
2. Access accounts: Okta, Slack, Google Workspace, Confluence, GitHub, Linear, and Redwood Console.
3. Join team orientation and meet manager: 30/60/90 goals discussion.
4. Complete security training and 2FA setup.
5. Setup local dev environment following the Quickstart guide: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates.

30/60/90 day onboarding goals (example):
- 30 days: Understand the product and infra, run local dev environment, complete 1 small bugfix or docs PR.
- 60 days: Own a small feature, participate in design reviews, and contribute to on-call docs.
- 90 days: Deliver a cross-team improvement, present learnings to the team, and have a development plan with the manager.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding:
- Provide clear goals and measures, schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 90 days, and ensure training and mentorship connections.

5) Internal tools & access guide

Primary tools (how we use them):
- Confluence (this space): canonical docs and runbooks - create pages under your team space and follow the doc template.
- Slack: primary async/sync chat; use public channels for project communications and private channels for sensitive items. Follow the Slack etiquette guide.
- GitHub: code hosting and PRs. Branch naming: feature/<ticket-number>-short-desc. Use required reviewers and CI checks.
- Linear: issue tracking and sprint planning; link PRs to Linear issues.
- Redwood Console: internal multi-tenant console for model/endpoint config, logs, and cost dashboards (access via Okta).
- PagerDuty: incident paging and on-call rotations. Integrations with Slack and Ops channels are enabled.
- Okta & SSO: single source for identity. All employees must enable SSO and 2FA.

Access & security expectations:
- Least privilege: request only the minimal roles needed for work. Use the access request form (Confluence link) and include business justification.
- Secrets & keys: never store secrets in plain text. Use Secrets Manager and follow the secure-sdlc policies.
- Remote access: if using corporate VPN, ensure device compliance and disk encryption.

Developer & infra quick links (examples):
- Dev quickstart: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Infra runbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks
- Oncall runbook and SLOs: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

6) Policies & escalation

Reporting: for HR issues, contact HRBP@redwood.com and People Ops. For security incidents, follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security runbook and page the security oncall.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Manager -> Director -> People Ops -> CEO (for critical cases).

Document maintenance & ownership
- Owner: people-ops (maintainer: Sophie Martinez).
- Review cadence: annual review; update after any benefits, leave, or major tool/process change.
- To propose changes: submit a doc PR or email people-ops@redwood.com with the proposed updates and rationale.

Appendix: Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: Who do I contact to change my equity grant?
A: Reach out to your manager and people-ops@redwood.com; compensation changes require Finance sign-off.

Q: I need a laptop replacement—what’s the process?
A: File a request in the IT ticketing system and include justification; People Ops will approve standard replacements per lifecycle policy.

Q: Where are detailed parental leave policies?
A: See Confluence > company-handbook > Benefits (linked above) for region-specific entitlements.

End of document. For operational runbooks, interview rubrics, and team-specific checklists see the linked pages in this space.
